content.text:
I migrated all three functions and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 696 bytes (min+gzip) with 87 bytes of own code.

I couldn't compare against the original. `lodash` isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` fails to build and type-check, and `npm run size -- src/module.ts` gives no number. I checked behaviour by reading the installed es-toolkit 1.53.2 declarations and sources and by running its `words` on sample strings.

| Function | Replacement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `words` from `es-toolkit/string` | I ran this on `"Id_MAX "`, `""`, `"a1b2"`, `"XMLHttp3D"`, `"ABCdef"`, `"foo-bar.baz 12ab"` and `"x__Y"`. It splits on case changes, acronyms and digits the way I expect lodash's `words` to for ASCII input, but I couldn't confirm that against lodash. |
| `byAge` | `groupBy` from `es-toolkit/array` | The main `groupBy` only accepts a function, so the adapter is `(row) => row.age` instead of `'age'`. The keys come out as strings, as before. |
| `isBlank` | `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty` | The main package has no `isEmpty`, only `isEmptyObject`. The compat `isEmpty` follows lodash's rules: `null`, numbers and booleans count as empty, and `""`, `[]` and `{}` are empty. |

`isEmpty` is a default import, because that subpath has no named export. I used the per-function path rather than `es-toolkit/compat`; that was 2 bytes smaller (696 vs 698).

No lodash import remains, and nothing was installed.
